Use case: compositing.
Asset type: full-viewport architectural editorial concept photograph for a luxury tile studio website. Wide landscape 16:9 composition, ultra-photorealistic, no typography.
Input image 1 is the exact owner-supplied Ivory geometry product reference: a pair of tall warm-ivory ornamental tile panels with fine looping lines, stacked central diamonds, small muted reflective inserts, fine bead-like ornament and a narrow center join. Preserve that exact pattern, original colors, two-panel proportions and subdued existing shallow relief. This is a precise product design reference, not loose inspiration.
Primary request: Create a beautiful sculptural private bathroom around the exact reference panel pair. Place the pair together as a generous, nearly front-facing vertical feature wall in the center of a warm limestone bathroom. Full-height pale plaster piers frame the panel composition without decorative added borders. An elegant pale travertine oval bathtub sits forward and to the right, largely outside the tile panel silhouette, with a slim dark-bronze floor tap. A long timber vanity with a limestone basin recedes at left. Clear full-wall glazing at far right gives quiet natural daylight, with a soft shadow on the stone floor.
Composition: Eye-level wide architectural editorial photograph, 28 mm lens, perfectly straight verticals and realistic perspective. The panel pair is the clearly legible central subject, covering about 40 percent of image width; both panels remain fully visible from top to bottom except minimal realistic floor transition. Generous architecture and believable depth, natural stone grain, convincingly tactile materials. Keep the bottom-left region calm for a small website caption, no text rendered in image.
Lighting: soft morning daylight, beautifully controlled pale tones, warm-neutral white balance, shadow detail retained, no golden filter.
Constraints: One complete luxurious bathroom scene, no montage, no collage, no frames, no people, no text, no logos, no watermark. Do not reinterpret the panel pattern, turn it into generic motifs, alter ivory to white/gold, stretch the panels, or invent extra relief. No dramatic zoom or wide-angle distortion. A fictional room visualization using supplied product imagery, not an installed-project photograph.
